title: Santino’s growth chamber: A chamber for studies with Aphelenchoides besseyi on plants
author: da Silva, Machado

steps.title: Fabricate structural frame
steps.instruction: Cut and bend galvanized steel tubes (7/8" diameter) to form the L‑shaped 2 mm plates (5 cm each side, 2 cm width) and the vaulted frame; fix the pieces with drilling screws and metal brackets to create a right foot 1.10 m above the bench (1.8 m from ground) and a central vault 1.26 m above the bench (1.96 m from ground) with 35° curves.

substeps.instruction: Shape and bend the steel tubes into the required L‑plates and arch pieces.
Assemble the pieces using drilling screws and metallic plates to secure the tubular bases to the bench.
Verify the heights of the right foot (1.10 m) and central vault (1.26 m).

steps.title: Build bench and install wire canvas
steps.instruction: Weld angle brackets (1 ¼" × 1 ⅛" galvanized steel) to form a bench 1.10 m wide, 0.73 m high, and 3.5 m long; add transverse cross‑beams every 0.583 m; weld a 12‑gauge (2.65 mm) galvanized steel wire mesh with 1‑inch openings to the free span of the assembled structure.

substeps.instruction: Weld angle brackets at the rectangle ends and centre to create the bench feet.
Weld cross‑beams at 0.583 m intervals along the length.
Attach the 12‑gauge wire canvas to the assembled frame.

steps.title: Install U‑profiles, curtains and wires
steps.instruction: Fix aluminum U‑profiles (1.10 m high) to the roof, front sides and movable side curtains; attach zig‑zag galvanized steel wire (12 mm, 1‑inch opening) to fasten the plastic; install C‑shaped wires at the right foot ends to hold curtains at 40 cm and 90 cm above the bench.

substeps.instruction: Mount U‑profiles on the roof, front, and side positions.
Stretch and fasten the plastic diffuser curtains with the zig‑zag wire.
Place C‑shaped wires to allow curtain positions at 40 cm and 90 cm.

steps.title: Install misting hydraulic system
steps.instruction: Connect a 100 L water tank to a 0.3 HP motor‑pump, a filter, and ½‑inch PVC piping fixed in the vault centre; install five Super Fogger 4 m sprinklers (flow 20.8 L h⁻¹) spaced 0.75 m apart and 0.25 m from each end, with threaded T‑fittings and couplings at 1.05 m height from the bench.

substeps.instruction: Place the water tank and pump in a convenient location.
Run ½‑inch PVC pipe along the vault centre and attach the filter.
Mount the five sprinklers at the specified spacing and height.
Secure all connections with threaded T‑fittings and couplings.

steps.title: Install electrical control system
steps.instruction: Mount a transformer (220 V → 24 VAC), 24 VAC relays, analog cyclic timer, promoter contactor, thermal relay, 20 A circuit breaker, output terminals and control buttons; wire the system to drive the pump, solenoid valves and misting schedule.

substeps.instruction: Connect the transformer to the mains (220 V) and obtain 24 VAC.
Wire relays, timer, contactor and thermal relay according to the schematic.
Install the 20 A circuit breaker and connect output terminals to the pump and valves.
Mount control buttons for on/off, manual, automatic and emergency functions.

steps.title: Program misting schedule and temperature control
steps.instruction: Set the water‑temperature controller to maintain a minimum of 25 °C; program the cyclic timer for a 24 h irrigation cycle with misting bursts of 5–30 s every 15 min (interval fixed, duration adjustable).

substeps.instruction: Adjust the temperature controller to activate heating when water drops below 25 °C.
Enter the misting parameters (5–30 s burst, 15 min interval) into the timer.
Select the 24 h continuous cycle mode.

steps.title: Add solenoid valves and temperature resistance
steps.instruction: Install a solenoid valve on the master hydraulic line for each chamber to allow independent programming; place a resistance heating element inside the water tank to keep water ≥25 °C.

substeps.instruction: Fit one solenoid valve per chamber between the main line and the sprinklers.
Connect each valve to its dedicated controller.
Mount the resistance heater in the tank and wire it to the temperature controller.

steps.title: Perform preliminary misting tests and adjust per crop
steps.instruction: Run the chamber and verify misting performance; adjust mist duration and interval according to crop‑specific tables: for Phaseolus vulgaris (4‑day old) use 5 s mist every 30 min; for Glycine max (7‑day old) 5 s every 30 min; for Gossypium hirsutum (15‑day old) 5 s every 30 min; increase mist time up to 30 s as plants grow to maintain leaf humidity.

substeps.instruction: Start the system with the initial 5 s mist per start for the first 15 days after germination.
Monitor leaf surface moisture and increase mist duration as needed (up to 30 s).
Record the optimal interval and duration for each crop as shown in Table 1.

steps.title: Prepare plants and inoculate with nematodes
steps.instruction: Grow soybean, cotton, common bean or tobacco plants; at 6 d (soybean), 10 d (common bean) or 20 d (cotton) after sowing, pipette 300 Aphelenchoides besseyi nematodes (suspended in water) into the soil near each plant stem.

substeps.instruction: Grow a pure A. besseyi culture on potato‑dextrose‑agar and prepare a suspension.
Measure 300 nematodes per plant (initial population, IP).
Inject the suspension into the soil close to the stem at the specified days after sowing.

steps.title: Operate chamber and monitor environment
steps.instruction: Run the misting program daily; record temperature and relative humidity inside and outside the chamber each day.

steps.title: Separate inoculated and non‑inoculated plants
steps.instruction: Install a plastic curtain fixed to the right central foot at 85 cm height to divide the chamber into two halves; place inoculated plants on one side and non‑inoculated plants on the other.

steps.title: Extract nematodes and calculate reproduction factor
steps.instruction: At 35 days after inoculation, extract nematodes from soil using an optimized Baermann funnel, from roots with the blender‑sieving method, and from shoots with blender‑sieving + Baermann; sum NNS, NNR and NNAT to obtain final population (FP) and compute RF = FP / IP.

substeps.instruction: Perform Baermann funnel extraction on soil samples (NNS).
Blend and sieve root tissue to count root nematodes (NNR).
Blend, sieve and Baermann‑extract shoot tissue for shoot nematodes (NNAT).
Add NNS + NNR + NNAT = FP; calculate RF = FP / IP.
